input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file only on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`) and then splits each line on "," without stripping a trailing carriage return. Files exported from Windows tools use CRLF line endings, so the header's last field ends up with a trailing "\r", which throws off the column match against the body rows and triggers the "errors.rowShape" error on row 1. The parser needs to normalize line endings (handle \r\n) before splitting into rows/columns.

text: This confirms the bug: splitting on "\n" only, not handling Windows CRLF line endings (\r\n), which would leave a trailing "\r" on the header fields causing column count/content mismatch — consistent with the new Windows export tool.
